findings.title: Revoke the outer capability when savepoint recovery fails
findings.cause: record_delivery_mail_no_effect and failExhausted rely on client.transaction for atomic caught-native-fault recovery. If a SQLite statement rolls back the entire transaction, ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT fails because the savepoint no longer exists. This cleanup failure escapes without revoking shared transactionState.active. The outbox per-statement guard checks only that token, not whether the transaction survived. A trusted host catching the fault can therefore issue further transactional operations that execute in SQLite autocommit.
reproducer: Real Bun 1.2.20 SQLite :memory:, production claims/outbox includes and exact extracted generated transaction emission; no deadline/retry configuration or compiler rebuild.
Commit an intent, claim maxInvocations=1, and commit possible_dispatch=1.
Install a fixture BEFORE INSERT trigger on __jadpo_delivery_dead_letters_v1 using SELECT RAISE(ROLLBACK, 'native whole transaction rollback').

Inside a new outer transaction call record_delivery_mail_no_effect with service_unavailable/providerAttempts=3/retryDelayMs=0; catch its transaction.savepoint.rollback fault (cause: no such savepoint: jadpo_sp_1).
Observe sqlite.inTransaction=false, then enqueue another unrelated intent through the same supposedly transactional client and insert an unrelated authority row.

Outer COMMIT fails. The exact emitted outer path correctly returns phase=commit/outcome=unknown/kind=unknown, but the unrelated intent and authority row are already durable. The original intent remains running with possible_dispatch=1 and no committed no-effect history.
findings.impact: The claimed caught-fault transaction containment is incomplete: a caught failed recovery permits outbox/authority writes outside the original transaction. Correct final unknown classification prevents blind replay but cannot undo autocommitted writes. This is an inherited generated transaction dependency exposed by the new atomic seam, not a defect in the normal no-effect SQL decision.
findings.requiredCorrection: Invalidate/poison the shared outer-attempt capability when savepoint recovery cannot be proved, and prevent further transactional SQL on the dead/uncertain transaction. Preserve unknown/no-blind-replay classification and add a generated-host regression that catches this failure and proves subsequent enqueue/mutation cannot autocommit. Do not merely change the final COMMIT mapping.
findings.limits: Confirmed with an explicit whole-transaction-rollback fixture, not a claim that ordinary constraint failures or every SQLITE_FULL error abort the whole transaction. A separate real SQLITE_FULL control preserved the outer transaction and recovered safely. PostgreSQL failed-cleanup behavior was inspected but not independently reproduced.

codeAssessment: Normal current-fence no-effect decision is sound under trusted-host provenance: per-key lock, running-state check, single materialized DB clock, exact current claim/generation and all three live absolute deadlines. possible_dispatch need not already be 1, allowing proved pre-dispatch failures; unknown/terminal intents never enter this path.

Eligible no-effect evidence is retained when SQL returns late, as with known acceptance. Provider no-effect proof is not undone by lease expiry after the guarded SQL. The decision is provisional until outer COMMIT acknowledgement; expiry before the SQL rejects it and preserves uncertainty.
History/reset/state/dead-letter sequencing is atomic for recovered savepoints and outer rollback, but failed savepoint cleanup has the blocking capability gap above.

Immutable max invocation and first-claim lifetime remain unchanged. New claims charge one fence/invocation before execution; exhaustion does not refund/reset. possible_dispatch recovery reaches unknown before budget exhaustion, so unknown never dead-letters merely for expiry/count.

Early and allocation-SQL retry delay gates persist across restart and prevent safe retries from overtaking the previous generation's retry_not_before. Same-key nonterminal FIFO remains in force; only known terminal states release it.

Invocations are bounded to signed 32-bit positive limits and providerAttempts to 0..3, so aggregate terminal count is bounded by 3*2147483647. SQL BIGINT generations stay native in comparisons/increments and are cast to text at JS seams, avoiding >2^53 fence aliasing. Signed BIGINT overflow is refused rather than reused.

Dead-letter stores fixed safe class/count/version/intent/generation/time, not raw diagnostics, payload, credentials or provider bodies. Caller-supplied delay is finite/nonnegative and calendar-checked, but neither bounded exponential policy nor full jitter selection is implemented here.

Both SQLite and PostgreSQL SQL branches were inspected: materialized clocks, correlated generation delay predicate, native BIGINT comparisons and aggregate count insert. Independent PostgreSQL execution was not performed.

retainedLimits: No approval of the whole RM-306 task, frozen ASYNC catalog's 18 executable traces, generated public jobs, compiler provenance/authority binding, worker heartbeat/dispatch/cancellation, scheduler, privileged resolve/replay or operator dead-letter API.

This is private trusted-host state only. Closed outcome shape/counts do not prove adapter provenance, transport no-dispatch or provider refusal. A host can forge the input today; only future compiler bindings may safely supply it. No provider calls or actual reference provider conformance were reviewed.

Selected retry delay is persisted, not policy-selected. Full jitter/exponential bounds, shared provider three-attempt/30-second elapsed budget, handler/payload compatibility and actual golden 3-invocation/1-hour job integration remain separate gates.

Default supported DB UTC semantics are trusted; no monotonic wall-clock, clock-regression, hard interruption, bounded query-return latency, commit-to-dispatch gap or exactly-once external effect guarantee. Known no-effect/success evidence retained after a late return still requires acknowledged COMMIT.

Existing compatible compiler-owned schema only. Lazy IF NOT EXISTS is not schema attestation, migration/drill support, collision immunity or validation of arbitrary corrupted/restored schemas. Fixture triggers model statement/recovery failures, not approval of altered production schemas.

Possible markers remain conservative through expiration/restart; unknown blocks FIFO and is never refunded or blindly replayed. The blocking failed-cleanup capability gap must be addressed independently of this safety policy.
Active-token checks reject stale views and callbacks but do not cancel already issued SQL or detached promises. Hosts must await all work before leaving the outer transaction.
Main's full supported gate remains release_equivalent=false with golden compile/behavior and other open gates; a green bounded storage suite cannot substitute for those requirements.
